summary: The calls support a small first-property setting set: configure 12–18-month lease terms and build a maintenance workflow around warranty review, technician skills, capacity, and a Warranty Managers group. Most discussions concern functionality and integrations—not catalog values—especially Power BI/data access, YieldStar/Arum, Ingrain websites, utilities, AI, forecasting, implementation phasing, and Greystar help-desk support. The latest calls make Greystar support the primary unresolved blocker and target the first 1,800 units around January 1.

functionality.product: Pilot property followed by tranches of five to seven properties and later retrofits
functionality.why: The client wants to prove the setup at one property, then roll properties in roughly 30-day waves. The latest plan targets about 1,800 units first, followed by about 3,500 units in Q2 and later existing-property retrofits.

turns.text: So let's talk a little bit about how the timing of resident utility works. And then I'll turn it over to Jackie or Janine if they've got other questions that they want to cover with you as far as product specific. I think Jackie specifically has some things she'd like to cover. But the way it works is the entrata core platform products are all going to go live at the same time. So if we use November as an example, let's say you take five properties live in November. The next month would be December that's when we would do your implementation of resident utilities. That's when you would provide all of the bills and all that information that we need in order to set it up the next month. Which would be in this example, January, that would be when your first pre bill would be ready for review. And then February one is when your first billing in entrata would occur. So just be aware that the rollout of resident utility does lag by about a month and a half behind the rest of the core products. Any questions there concerns? I think that's pretty typical in the industry. I don't know that we're unusual there, but.

callsUsed.title: Entrata/Yardly by Taylor Morrison Demo Prep
callsUsed.brief: The call focused on Taylor Morrison's interest in Entrata as a potential replacement for their current property management systems due to data accessibility issues with Graystar's use of RealPage and Yardi. Taylor Morrison is seeking a unified platform with open API feeds to improve data visibility and reporting, particularly for their Power BI tool used for communicating with JV partners and C-suite executives. The upcoming summit will explore Entrata's capabilities, including data intelligence, revenue management, and AI components, with a focus on how Entrata can streamline their reporting processes and integrate with their existing systems.

callsUsed.brief: The call involved a discussion about improving implementation fee justification, shifting scoping responsibilities, and pursuing a potential deal with MEB in Brighton. The team also connected with Nicole, the new asset manager for Taylor Morrison, to discuss their Yardi and Entrata preferences and the challenges of system changes. Ultimately, the call with Taylor Morrison was rescheduled for Friday due to the absence of key players, Emily and Rachel.

callsUsed.title: Entrata/Yardly by Taylor Morrison Utilities Scoping Call
callsUsed.brief: The Entrata team met with Taylor Morrison and Graystar representatives to discuss the implementation of Entrata's resident utility product and other services for their build-to-rent properties, focusing on scoping the project, addressing concerns about the transition from Conservice, and planning for an upcoming onsite meeting to explore the software's functionality and integration with their existing systems. Key discussion points included utility billing processes, data migration, reporting needs, and the overall resident lifecycle within the Entrata platform, with a strong emphasis on streamlining processes and improving budgeting accuracy. The team also discussed the possibility of leveraging Graystar's existing Entrata setup as a baseline for implementation.
